100: The Great Jahy Will Not Be Defeated! by Wakame Konbu (Square Enix) is a cheerful workplace comedy with a fantasy twist. Jahy was the proud second-in-command of the Dark Realm until a magical girl shattered its mana crystal, leaving her stuck in the human world in a tiny body, and now she rents a cramped apartment and works at a neighborhood bar while plotting her comeback. It's a light, goofy read for anyone who enjoys a fallen villain trying very hard at everyday life.
101: Hell Mode by Hamuo (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure about a gamer who wants a real challenge. Bored with games that are too easy, a hardcore player picks the hardest possible setting and finds himself reborn in another world as Allen, a peasant boy with the rare Summoner class. Leveling up is brutally slow, but he loves the grind. Readers who enjoy careful stat-building and a lead who plans every step will feel right at home.
102: Her Majesty's Dog by Mick Takeuchi (Go! Comi) is a supernatural romance with a gentle, mysterious mood. Amane comes from a remote village and has the power to make her words come true, and she moves to the city for school with Hyoue, a dog spirit who takes human form and serves as her loyal guardian. The pairing of a quiet heroine and her devoted protector makes this a good fit for fans of yokai stories with a romantic thread.
103: Battle Angel Alita: Mars Chronicle by Yukito Kishiro (Kodansha) is a science fiction action series that returns to the world of Battle Angel Alita. This chapter of the saga goes back to Alita's early life on Mars, long before she woke up in the Scrapyard, and follows the events that shaped the girl she became. Kishiro's detailed cyborg designs and hard-hitting fights are all here. Longtime fans will enjoy filling in Alita's past, and it rewards readers who like dense, thoughtful sci-fi.
104: No. 6 by Atsuko Asano (Kodansha) is a science fiction drama set in a city that looks like a perfect utopia. Shion is a gifted boy living a privileged life in No. 6 until, on a stormy night when he is twelve, he shelters a wounded fugitive named Nezumi. That one choice costs him his place in the city and leads him to see what lies beneath its polished surface. It's a moving story about friendship and questioning the world you were raised in.
106: Hikaru no Go by Yumi Hotta (Viz Media) is a coming-of-age story about the ancient board game Go. Sixth grader Hikaru Shindo is poking around his grandfather's attic when he finds an old Go board haunted by Sai, the ghost of a master player from centuries ago. Sai just wants to play again, and Hikaru slowly gets drawn into the game himself. You don't need to know the rules to enjoy it; the rivalries and growth carry the story.
108: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess by Akira Himekawa (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure based on the beloved video game. Link is a quiet young ranch hand in the village of Ordon, carrying scars from his past. When a strange twilight spreads across Hyrule, he is transformed into a wolf and meets Midna, a sharp-tongued imp with her own agenda. This adaptation gives Link a voice and backstory, making it a treat for game fans and newcomers alike.
109: Omamori Himari by Milan Matra (Yen Press) is a supernatural action comedy with plenty of fan service. On his sixteenth birthday, Yuto Amakawa learns that he comes from a family of demon slayers and that the charm protecting him has worn off. Now monsters are after him, and his guardian turns out to be Himari, a cat spirit who fights with a sword. It's a lively harem series for fans of yokai battles mixed with romantic comedy.
111: How Not to Summon a Demon Lord by Yukiya Murasaki (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy comedy with plenty of fan service. Takuma is a shy gamer who plays as the fearsome demon lord Diablo. When he is summoned into a world that looks just like his game, he has his avatar's body and power, but none of the confidence, so he acts like Diablo full-time. Fans of overpowered heroes and awkward social mishaps will have fun with this one.
113: Hyper Police by Minoru Tachikawa (Tokyopop) is a fast, funny action series set in a future where monsters and demi-humans far outnumber humans. Natsuki is a cat-girl bounty hunter working for a small, struggling agency in a rough part of Tokyo. Between rival hunters, dangerous targets, and an empty bank account, every job is a scramble. Readers who enjoy scrappy heroes, quick humor, and creature-filled cityscapes will find a lot to like.
116: I Think I Turned My Childhood Friend into a Girl by Norio Sakurai (Seven Seas) is a light romantic comedy. Itsuki jokingly tells his best friend Mikoto, who has a very pretty face, that he'd look great as a girl. Mikoto takes it to heart and starts showing up to school dressed as one, and Itsuki suddenly can't stop noticing him. It's a sweet, silly story for readers who enjoy cross-dressing comedies and friendships that slowly turn into something more.
117: The Saint's Magic Power Is Omnipotent by Yuka Tachibana (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy romance. Sei is an overworked office worker who is suddenly summoned to another world as its legendary Saint, only to be brushed aside when the prince chooses another girl. Left on her own, she happily takes a job at a research institute making potions, and her work starts turning out far stronger than anyone expected. It's a relaxing read for fans of slow-burn romance and capable heroines.
118: Bloody Monday by Ryou Ryumon (Kodansha) is a high-tension thriller full of hacking and conspiracy. Fujimaru Takagi seems like an ordinary high schooler, but he is secretly a genius hacker who helps his father's government intelligence agency. When a mysterious group plots a terror attack on Tokyo, Fujimaru is pulled into a race against time where anyone could be a traitor. Readers who love twisty spy stories and cyber-thrillers will race through it.
119: I'm the Villainess, So I'm Taming the Final Boss by Sarasa Nagase (Yen Press) is a fantasy romantic comedy. When her prince fiance breaks their engagement in public, Aileen suddenly remembers her past life and realizes she is the villainess of an otome game. Every route ends badly for her, so she comes up with a bold plan: win over Claude, the demon king who is the game's final boss. Fans of clever, determined heroines and villainess stories will enjoy it.
120: Bottom-Tier Character Tomozaki by Yuki Yaku (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy about learning to play the game of life. Fumiya Tomozaki is the top-ranked player of a popular fighting game but a total loner at school, convinced that real life is a broken game. Then he meets his online rival in person and discovers it's Aoi Hinami, the most perfect girl in his class. She decides to coach him, step by step, in a story that's warm, funny, and surprisingly thoughtful.
121: Peach Girl by Miwa Ueda (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance full of high school drama. Momo Adachi has tanned skin and light hair from years on the swim team, so classmates assume she is a party girl, even though she only has eyes for her quiet crush, Toji. Her so-called best friend Sae keeps stirring up trouble, and the flirty Kairi complicates things further. It's a juicy, emotional read for anyone who loves love triangles and frenemy schemes.
122: Im: Great Priest Imhotep by Makoto Morishita (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series with an ancient Egyptian twist. Imhotep, a powerful priest from Egypt's distant past, awakens in modern-day Japan with one mission: to hunt down the Magai, beings that steal the power of the old gods. A local high school girl soon gets swept into his fight. It's a fun mix of mythology, magic battles, and fish-out-of-water humor.
124: Persona 3 by Shuji Sogabe (Udon) is a supernatural action story based on the popular video game. A quiet transfer student arrives at Gekkoukan High and learns that there is a hidden hour between one day and the next, when monsters called Shadows roam. He joins a group of students who fight them by summoning their inner selves, called Personas. Game fans will enjoy seeing the cast come to life, and newcomers get a moody, stylish school adventure.
125: Buso Renkin by Nobuhiro Watsuki (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy from the creator of Rurouni Kenshin. High schooler Kazuki Muto is killed while trying to save a girl from a monster, but she revives him by replacing his heart with an alchemical core called a kakugane. Now he can summon a weapon of his own and is drawn into a hidden war against man-eating homunculi. It's energetic and big-hearted, with quirky villains and lots of heart.
127: Interviews with Monster Girls by Petos (Kodansha) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy. Tetsuo Takahashi is a high school biology teacher who has always been fascinated by demi-humans, people with traits from folklore. When several students turn out to be a vampire, a dullahan, and a snow woman, he starts listening to what everyday life is like for them. It's kind, funny, and thoughtful, perfect for readers who want a cozy story about understanding others.
128: Inu-Yasha: A Feudal Fairy Tale by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure full of action, humor, and romance. Kagome Higurashi is an ordinary schoolgirl until she is pulled down an old well at her family's shrine and lands in feudal Japan. There she frees Inu-Yasha, a hot-tempered half-demon, and accidentally shatters the magical Shikon Jewel, so now the two must work together to gather the shards. It's a classic for good reason.
129: Candy and Cigarettes by Tomonori Inoue (Seven Seas) is a gritty action thriller. Raizo Shiba is a retired police officer in his sixties who is struggling to support his grandchild, so he takes a job with a secret organization that turns out to be a ring of assassins. His new partner is Miharu, an eleven-year-old girl who is a skilled killer. It's violent and dark, with an odd-couple bond at its center, for readers who enjoy hard-edged crime stories.
130: Captain Harlock: Dimensional Voyage by Leiji Matsumoto (Seven Seas) is a space opera that retells the classic Captain Harlock story. Earth has grown lazy and complacent, and no one is ready for a new threat from beyond the stars. Only the outlaw Harlock and the crew of his ship, the Arcadia, are willing to fight, and young Tadashi Daiba joins them after losing his father. It's a stirring, old-school adventure for sci-fi fans and newcomers to Matsumoto's universe.
131: Though I Am an Inept Villainess by Satsuki Nakamura (Seven Seas) is a palace fantasy comedy with a body-swap twist. Kou Reirin is the most beloved consort candidate in the imperial court, while Shu Keigetsu is the most despised. Keigetsu uses forbidden magic to switch bodies with Reirin, expecting her rival to fall apart, but instead the cheerful Reirin is delighted with her healthy new body. It's sweet, clever, and full of court intrigue and close friendship between women.
132: Threads of Time by Mi Young Noh (Tokyopop) is a historical fantasy set during the Mongol invasions of Korea. Moon Bin is a modern teenage boy who keeps having strange dreams about life in the thirteenth century. After an accident, he wakes up living that life as the son of a Korean noble, caught in a time of war. It's a sweeping story of friendship, loyalty, and danger for readers who enjoy history mixed with adventure.
134: Kagetora by Akira Segami (Del Rey) is a romantic comedy with ninja action. Kagetora is a skilled young ninja sent to serve and protect Yuki, the heir of a respected martial arts family. The trouble is that Yuki is clumsy, gentle, and hopeless at fighting, and she wants him to teach her ninja skills, while he tries very hard not to fall for her. Fans of sweet romance and lighthearted action will enjoy it.
135: Clockwork Planet by Yuu Kamiya (Kodansha) is a science fiction adventure set on an Earth rebuilt entirely out of gears. High schooler Naoto Miura is an outcast who loves machines more than anything. One day a coffin crashes through his roof, holding a broken automaton named RyuZU, and repairing her pulls him into a plot that could decide the fate of the planet. Its steampunk world is a delight for fans of mechanical fantasy.
136: Psychic Academy by Katsu Aki (Tokyopop) is a science fiction school story in a world where psychic powers are common. Ai Shiomi is the younger brother of a famous hero, but his own abilities are weak, and he enrolls at a special academy for psychics feeling the pressure of his brother's name. There he struggles with his studies, his powers, and his feelings for two very different girls. It's a mix of romance, growing up, and psychic battles.
137: Toradora! by Yuyuko Takemiya (Seven Seas) is a high school romantic comedy. Ryuji Takasu is a kind, tidy boy whose sharp eyes make everyone think he's a delinquent, while Taiga Aisaka is tiny but has a fierce temper that's earned her the nickname "Palmtop Tiger." When they discover each has a crush on the other's best friend, they team up to help each other. It's funny and heartfelt, with a cast that feels like real teenagers.
138: Trillion Game by Riichiro Inagaki (Viz Media) is a business drama with a gambler's swagger. Haru is a smooth-talking risk-taker who can charm anyone, and Gaku is a shy computer genius who can build anything. The two old friends make a wild promise to earn a trillion dollars together, starting with almost nothing, and the bluffing is half the fun. It's great for readers who like underdog schemes and fast-paced strategy.
139: Kakuriyo: Bed & Breakfast for Spirits by Waco Ioka (Viz Media) is a cozy fantasy romance with lots of good food. Aoi Tsubaki inherited her grandfather's ability to see spirits, and also, it turns out, his debt. An ogre carries her off to the spirit world and tells her she must marry him to settle it, but Aoi refuses and decides to work off the debt herself by cooking for spirits. It's a warm, charming read for fans of yokai stories.
142: Reborn as a Space Mercenary by Shinichi Matsui (Seven Seas) is a science fiction adventure with a gamer's spirit. A man who loved playing a space simulation game wakes up inside its world, along with his powerful ship. With nothing else to rely on, he decides to make a living as a mercenary, picking up jobs, fighting pirates, and gaining unlikely companions along the way. It's a fun, easygoing read for fans of spaceship battles and isekai adventures.
143: Ubel Blatt by Etorouji Shiono (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy revenge story. Years ago, seven heroes were sent to stop an invading army, but three of them were betrayed and killed by their own companions, who then took the credit. Now a mysterious young swordsman named Koinzell sets out to hunt down the false heroes who rule the land. It's violent and mature, with striking art, for readers who enjoy grim fantasy and stories of vengeance.
144: Vampire Hunter D by Hideyuki Kikuchi (DMP) is a gothic horror adventure based on the classic novels. Far in the future, the world is a wasteland ruled by vampire aristocrats called Nobles, and humans live in fear. D is a quiet, half-human, half-vampire hunter who travels from town to town taking jobs to destroy them, drawn here in dark, moody art. It's a great pick for fans of vampire stories and post-apocalyptic westerns.
145: Kitchen Princess by Miyuki Kobayashi (Kodansha) is a sweet shojo romance about cooking. Najika is an orphan with an incredible sense of taste and a big heart. Years ago, a boy comforted her with a dish of flan, and she has been looking for her "flan prince" ever since, and her search leads her to an elite academy, where her cooking wins friends and makes rivals. It's heartwarming and full of food, with a dash of drama.
147: Rosario + Vampire by Akihisa Ikeda (Viz Media) is a supernatural comedy with lots of action. Tsukune Aono is an average guy who accidentally enrolls at Yokai Academy, a school for monsters where humans are not allowed. On his first day he meets Moka Akashiya, a sweet girl who turns out to be a vampire, and now he has to keep his secret and survive. It's a fun mix of harem comedy and monster battles.
148: Descendants of Darkness by Yoko Matsushita (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery series. Asato Tsuzuki works for the Ministry of Hades as a shinigami, an agent of death who guides souls that won't move on. He is cheerful and easygoing on the surface, and paired with a prickly new partner, Hisoka Kurosaki, who has his own dark past, to investigate strange deaths. It's moody, emotional, and stylish, for readers who like detective stories with a gothic edge.
149: Let This Grieving Soul Retire by Rai Hebino (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy built on misunderstandings. Krai Andrey leads one of the most famous treasure-hunting parties in the land, and everyone believes he is a brilliant mastermind. In truth, he is weak, timid, and would love nothing more than to quit, yet every offhand remark he makes gets taken as a stroke of genius. It's a fun read for fans of accidental heroes and gentle humor.
150: Level 1 Demon Lord and One Room Hero by Toufu (Seven Seas) is a relaxed fantasy comedy. Years after being defeated, the Demon Lord is revived at level one and sets out to find the hero who beat him. He finds him living in a tiny apartment, unemployed and playing video games all day, so with nowhere else to go, the Demon Lord moves in and starts keeping house. It's a cozy, funny slice of life for fans of fantasy parody.
151: Do You Love Your Mom and Her Two-Hit Multi-Target Attacks? by Dachima Inaka (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy with a twist on the isekai formula. High schooler Masato Oosuki is chosen to test a new game that sends players into a fantasy world. He dreams of becoming a hero, but his mother, Mamako, comes along too and turns out to be far stronger than he is. It's a silly, good-natured story about family that pokes fun at gaming tropes.
152: Sasaki and Peeps by Buncololi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy about a middle-aged office worker who stumbles into adventure. Sasaki buys a little sparrow to keep him company, and the bird turns out to be Peeps, a great sage from another world. Peeps lets Sasaki travel back and forth between Earth and that world, where he starts a side business, though he soon gets drawn into strange events at home too. It's laid-back and genre-bending.
155: Magical Explorer by Iris (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure with a gamer's twist. A man who knew his favorite fantasy game inside and out wakes up reborn as Kousuke Takioto, a minor side character whose job is just to support the hero. Using everything he remembers about the game, he decides to become as strong as possible on his own terms. It's a fun read for fans of game-world stories and clever strategy.
156: Maid Sama! by Hiro Fujiwara (Tokyopop) is a shojo romantic comedy. Misaki Ayuzawa is the tough student council president at a school that used to be all boys, but she has a secret: to help her family, she works part-time at a maid cafe, and when the popular, carefree Takumi Usui finds out, he keeps her secret and keeps showing up. It's funny, charming, and full of heart.
159: Emma by Kaoru Mori (CMX) is a gentle historical romance set in Victorian London. Emma is a quiet, hardworking maid who catches the eye of William Jones, the eldest son of a wealthy merchant family. Their feelings for each other grow, but the class divide between them is hard to ignore. Mori's detailed art brings the era to life, making this a lovely pick for fans of slow romance and period drama.
161: Fate/stay night by Type-Moon (Tokyopop) is an action fantasy based on the hit visual novel. Shirou Emiya is a high schooler with a bit of magic training and a strong sense of justice. One night he stumbles into the Holy Grail War, a secret battle between mages and the legendary heroes they summon. Near death, he summons a hero of his own, the knight Saber, in a story full of intense magic battles.
162: Shibuya Goldfish by Hiroumi Aoi (Yen Press) is a survival horror thriller. One day, Tokyo's busy Shibuya district is suddenly sealed off from the outside world, and giant man-eating goldfish begin swimming through the air. A high school boy trapped inside must find a way to protect the people he cares about and figure out what is happening before they are all eaten. It's tense and strange, for readers who enjoy monster panic stories.
165: Are You Alice? by Ikumi Katagiri (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy mystery inspired by Alice in Wonderland. A young man with no memory of his past suddenly finds himself in Wonderland, where he is given the name Alice and a single command: kill the White Rabbit, while the Mad Hatter, the Cheshire Cat, and other familiar faces all seem to know more than they say. It's a stylish, twisty retelling for fans of unusual takes on classic stories.
166: Kakuriyo: Bed & Breakfast for Spirits by Waco Ioka (Viz Media) is a cozy fantasy romance with lots of good food. Aoi Tsubaki inherited her grandfather's ability to see spirits, and also, it turns out, his debt. An ogre carries her off to the spirit world and tells her she must marry him to settle it, but Aoi refuses and decides to work off the debt herself by cooking for spirits. It's a warm, charming read for fans of yokai stories.
167: Please Go Home, Miss Akutsu! by Yuu Nagira (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy. Ooyama is a quiet high school boy who just wants to spend his free time at home. For some reason, Akutsu, a tough-looking girl from his school, keeps showing up at his house and making herself comfortable, though she is clearly flustered around him. It's a light, teasing story for fans of slow-burn romance.
169: Iron Wok Jan! by Shinji Saijyo (Comics One) is a cooking battle series full of attitude. Jan Akiyama was trained in Chinese cooking by his legendary chef grandfather, and he is brilliant and very cocky about it. When he takes a job at a famous Tokyo restaurant, he clashes with the owner's granddaughter Kiriko, a talented chef in her own right. It's loud, competitive, and full of mouthwatering dishes for fans of food manga.
170: Inu x Boku SS by Cocoa Fujiwara (Yen Press) is a supernatural romantic comedy. Ririchiyo Shirakiin comes from a powerful family and has a sharp tongue she can't seem to control. Hoping to live on her own, she moves into an exclusive apartment building where every resident gets a personal Secret Service agent, and hers is Soushi Miketsukami, a devoted young man who is also a fox spirit. It's sweet, quirky, and full of colorful yokai residents.
171: The Most Heretical Last Boss Queen by Tenichi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy story about rewriting your fate. At eight years old, Princess Pride Royal Ivy remembers her past life and realizes she is the cruel villain and final boss of an otome game. In the game, she grows up to ruin countless lives, including her own, so she sets out to become a kind and worthy queen instead. It's heartfelt and earnest.
172: Konohana Kitan by Sakuya Amano (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy slice of life. Yuzu is a cheerful young fox girl who has just started working at Konohanatei, an inn for spirits and gods. She is eager to learn, but everything is new, and each chapter brings a new guest and a small, warm story. It's soothing and pretty, a good pick for readers who want something calm and kind.
173: My Quiet Blacksmith Life in Another World by Tamamaru (J-Novel Club) is a relaxing fantasy slice of life. After dying in an accident, a man is reborn in another world as Eizo, with a gift for crafting and blacksmithing. Wanting a peaceful life, he builds a forge deep in a forest that most people avoid, where a few unexpected visitors soon become companions. It's a calm, cozy read for fans of crafting, home life, and found family.
174: Tune by Derek Kirk Kim (First Second) is a funny, offbeat science fiction graphic novel. Andy Go is a young art school dropout who needs a job and has no idea what to do with his life. Then he gets an unusual offer: live as an exhibit in an alien zoo in a parallel universe, in exchange for a good paycheck. It's sharp, awkward, and very relatable, for readers who enjoy humor about growing up.
175: The Executioner and Her Way of Life by Mato Sato (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy adventure. In a world where people from Japan are sometimes summoned with dangerous powers, Menou works in secret as an executioner whose job is to kill them. Her newest target is Akari, a cheerful girl who seems impossible to kill, so Menou travels with her while she looks for a way. It's an intense, emotional story about duty and an unlikely bond.
176: A Business Proposal by Narak (Ize Press) is a lively office romantic comedy based on a popular webtoon. Shin Ha-ri agrees to go on a blind date in her friend's place, planning to act so badly that the man will leave. The problem is that her date turns out to be Kang Tae-mu, the CEO of her own company, and he wants to marry her. It's funny and sweet, perfect for fans of K-dramas and fake-dating stories.
178: Sunshine Sketch by Ume Aoki (Yen Press) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy. Yuno has just started at an art high school and moves into the Hidamari Apartments, right across the street. Her neighbors are fellow art students, and together they share meals, worry about assignments, and enjoy the small moments of everyday life. It's relaxing, warm, and funny, perfect for anyone who wants a calm, cozy read.
181: After School Nightmare by Setona Mizushiro (Go! Comi) is a psychological drama with a supernatural edge. Mashiro Ichijo is a high school student who lives as a boy while hiding a secret about his body, and he is placed in a mysterious class that meets only in dreams, where students battle each other in shared nightmares to earn their graduation. It's unsettling and thought-provoking, for readers who like stories about identity, fear, and growing up.
182: Sword Art Online Progressive by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series that retells the story of Sword Art Online from the very beginning. Thousands of players are trapped inside a virtual reality game where dying in the game means dying in real life. This version follows Kirito and Asuna as they fight their way through Aincrad one floor at a time, starting on the first. It fills in many details fans have long wanted to see.
183: Tactics by Sakura Kinoshita (ADV) is a supernatural comedy set in early twentieth-century Japan. Kantaro Ichinomiya is a folklorist who can see yokai and spirits. He frees a powerful tengu named Haruka, who becomes his companion, and the two take on jobs exorcising troublesome spirits while Kantaro looks for answers about his past. It's playful and charming, for fans of yokai stories with a sense of humor.
184: Akame ga Kill! Zero by Takahiro and Kei Toru (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action prequel to Akame ga Kill! Long before she joined Night Raid, Akame was sold as a child along with her sister and trained to become an elite assassin for the Empire. It's violent and gripping, a strong pick for fans of the original who want to see Akame's past.
185: Genshiken by Kio Shimoku (Del Rey) is a comedy about otaku culture. College freshman Kanji Sasahara is a secret anime and manga fan who finally finds his people when he joins the Society for the Study of Modern Visual Culture. The club spends its time playing games, arguing about anime, and making comics, even after a non-fan starts tagging along with her boyfriend. It's funny and honest, for anyone who has ever been a fan.
187: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation by Rifujin na Magonote (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure that helped shape the isekai genre. A thirty-four-year-old shut-in who wasted his life dies in an accident and is reborn in a world of magic as Rudeus Greyrat, with all his memories intact. Determined to live properly this time, he starts training in magic as a small child. It's a sprawling story of growth and second chances.
188: Alice 19th by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance. Alice Seno is a shy girl who lives in the shadow of her popular older sister. One day she saves a strange rabbit from a car, and it gives her the ability to use Lotis Words, magical words that can reach the hearts of others, and soon she must learn to use them. It's sweet and dramatic, from the creator of Fushigi Yugi.
189: Alice and Zoroku by Tetsuya Imai (Seven Seas) is a heartwarming fantasy slice of life. Sana is a young girl with an unusual power called the Dreams of Alice, which lets her turn her imagination into reality. After escaping from a research facility, she meets Zoroku, a grumpy old florist who takes her in, and their unlikely bond is the heart of the story. It's charming and kind, with just enough action to keep things exciting.
190: Tenjho Tenge by Oh! Great (CMX) is a martial arts action series with lots of fan service. Souichiro Nagi and his friend Bob Makihara transfer to Toudou Academy, planning to take over the school. Instead, they run straight into the Juken Club, a group of skilled fighters who have their own reasons for battling the school's powerful Executive Council. Its intense, beautifully drawn fights make it a good pick for readers who like gritty action.
191: Girls Bravo by Mario Kaneda (Tokyopop) is a fan service-heavy romantic comedy. Yukinari Sasaki is a timid boy with a strange problem: he breaks out in hives whenever a girl touches him. One day he falls into another world called Seiren, where women far outnumber men, and meets Miharu, a cheerful girl whose touch doesn't make him break out. It's silly and lighthearted, for fans of harem comedies.
192: The Angel Next Door Spoils Me Rotten by Saekisan (Yen Press) is a gentle romance about two neighbors. Amane Fujimiya is a lazy high schooler who lives alone, and Mahiru Shiina is the most admired girl at school, known as an angel, and she happens to live next door. After Amane lends her his umbrella on a rainy day, she starts cooking for him. It's slow and cozy, for readers who love sweet romance.
193: Anne Happy by Cotoji (Yen Press) is a cute school comedy. Ann Hanakoizumi is so unlucky that she gets hit by everything from flying birds to falling trees. She and a group of other girls with similarly hopeless luck are placed in a special class meant to teach them how to be happy. It's silly, sweet, and upbeat, for fans of cheerful slice-of-life stories.
194: The Disappearance of Nagato Yuki-chan by Nagaru Tanigawa (Yen Press) is a gentle romantic comedy set in an alternate version of the Haruhi Suzumiya world. Here Yuki Nagato is not an alien, but a shy, ordinary girl who runs the school literature club. She has a crush on Kyon, the boy who just joined. It's a sweet, low-key spin-off for longtime Haruhi fans and newcomers alike.
197: Happy Sugar Life by Tomiyaki Kagisora (Yen Press) is a dark psychological horror story. Satou Matsuzaka is a popular high school girl who has never understood love, until she meets Shio, a little girl she takes home to live with her. Satou is determined to protect the life they share in her apartment, and she is willing to do anything at all to keep it secret. It's disturbing and gripping, for readers who like unsettling stories.
198: Harukana Receive by Nyoijizai (Seven Seas) is a sports slice of life about beach volleyball. Haruka Ozora moves from Tokyo to Okinawa to live with her grandmother and her cousin Kanata, who used to play beach volleyball but quit, and Haruka's enthusiasm draws her back to the sand as partners. It's upbeat, fun, and full of summer energy, perfect for fans of friendship and sports stories.
